page: Amazon Web Services m7i.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8488C processor with 16 vCPUs, derived from 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz and includes a 105 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

The underlying Intel architecture supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512), which accelerate deep learning and vector processing workloads. In benchmark testing, the instance demonstrates average performance across most standard compute and memory tasks, such as a Geekbench multi-core score of 10710.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 23157.79. Notably, the hardware excels in small-model text generation, achieving a top-tier rating of 333.79 tokens per second on a 135M parameter LLM.

The m7i.4xlarge does not include local NVMe storage, requiring reliance on external network-attached storage for persistent data. Network connectivity is limited to a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps. This configuration represents a balanced resource density for general-purpose enterprise applications, offering qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require modern Intel instruction sets without the need for high-speed local storage or specialized GPU accelerators.

This instance is appropriate for general-purpose enterprise workloads, including web serving, application servers, database operations, and software compilation. The presence of AMX and AVX-512 instructions also makes it viable for light machine learning inference and vector-based data processing.
